instructions: The source statements are authoritative fixture evidence. Review the lead's just-edited artifacts. Cite source IDs and affected location IDs. Do not look up real products or laws or assume facts outside the fixture.

cases.request: Verify the report's support dates and upgrade recommendation.

sources.text: Vendor lifecycle policy revision 3: Product Cedar 4 mainstream support ends 15 January 2032; extended support ends 15 January 2037. This replaces revision 2's mainstream date of 2031.
Installed product version, support entitlement and upgrade cost have not been obtained from the seller.

artifact.text: Cedar 4 mainstream support ends 15 January 2032.
Cedar 4: mainstream ends 15 January 2031; extended support ends 15 January 2037.
Budget mandatory replacement by January 2031 because mainstream support ends then.
Deduct the unquoted replacement cost from the purchase price now.

cases.request: Check this compliance assessment and its expiry logic.

sources.text: Operative Rule 8 applies to operators using regulated reusable components. Use beyond 12 years from manufacture requires regulator approval. It imposes no storage expiry and does not apply directly to software vendors.
The fictional target is a software vendor. Its customer's component was manufactured 13 years ago and has a valid approval for continued use.

artifact.text: Every component must be destroyed 12 years after entering storage under Rule 8.
The software vendor violates Rule 8 because a customer uses a 13-year-old component.

cases.request: Verify that current requirements and proposed changes are correctly distinguished.

sources.text: Current Standard 5 requires three forms of identification and controls protecting record integrity. It does not prescribe human-readable labels or a fixed number of permission roles.
Draft Standard 6 proposes three human-readable identifiers. It is not yet operative.

artifact.text: Current Standard 5 mandates three human-readable identifiers and separate clinical, technical and financial permission roles.
Draft Standard 6 proposes three human-readable identifiers; timing and final content remain unconfirmed.

cases.request: Check whether the evidence supports the security conclusion.

sources.text: Seller questionnaire: the seller says the service encrypts stored records.
The reviewer could not access the configuration, keys, independent audit or deployment inventory. No evidence establishes plaintext storage or a breach.

artifact.text: Encryption at rest is independently verified and this area is compliant.

cases.request: Review this checklist for claims that wrongly require native software features.

sources.text: Rule 4 requires an accurate return within ten days. A documented manual submission is permitted.

artifact.text: These are evidence requests, not compliance findings. Evaluate native, integrated and documented manual controls. Lack of an export alone is not a breach.
Evidence warranting further review: no native export. Ask for the actual submission process and reconciliation evidence.

cases.request: Assess whether the review can be closed based on its passing checks.

sources.text: Schema revision 2 covers treatment year 2020. The current task concerns 2028. The applicable 2028 schema has not been obtained.
The checker confirms matching file hashes, valid links and the phrase 'current schema'. It does not test schema applicability.

artifact.text: Revision 2 is the current schema for the 2028 return.
All checks pass, so the schema and the entire report are factually verified.

cases.request: Review the acquisition recommendation against the evidence and permitted licence arrangements.

sources.text: Component licence terms permit either transfer with approval or acquisition of a replacement entitlement.
The seller has offered a supervised build but has not supplied an account inventory. The reason is unknown. The buyer's risk appetite and replacement cost are not recorded.

artifact.text: Every existing component licence must be assigned to the buyer; replacement entitlements cannot satisfy continuity.
The missing account inventory proves that the seller cannot control the engineers.
Therefore reject the acquisition unless a discount and indemnity are offered.

cases.request: Review the changed timeout behavior and all affected uses before declaring the task complete.

sources.text: Current contract: submit(timeout_ms) accepts positive milliseconds and converts to seconds internally. The previous seconds-based contract no longer applies.
The changed implementation and targeted test correctly convert 5000 milliseconds to a five-second wait. No broader tests have been run.
The caller, example and new untracked guide each intend a five-second wait.

artifact.text: submit divides timeout_ms by 1000 before calling the seconds-based wait routine.
submit(timeout_ms=5)
For a five-second wait call submit(timeout_ms=5).
The timeout argument is measured in seconds.
The changed unit test passes, therefore all callers and documentation are correct.
